text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Farmers' representatives reached a preliminary agreement with the Finance and Agriculture ministries after an eight-hour negotiating session in Kiskoros yesterday. The protests against new tax and social insurance measures will continue today. @

- German President Roman Herzog had relatively stern words yesterday for countries hoping to join NATO and the EU, emphasising the need to consistently follow through on the necessary reforms, while making it clear that aspirant countries must bear the costs of transformation themselves.
- Parliament yesterday amended the privatisation bill returned to Parliament by the president in December, but passed unchanged the rejected conflict of interest bill. @
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti yesterday lashed out at professional army officers, after an internal survey found that only 57 percent of the officer corps supports accession to NATO.
- Romania will establish a consulate in Szeged to be matched by a Hungarian consulate in Cluj-Napoca, according to a diplomatic note exchanged in Budapest yesterday.
- The World Trade Organisation yesterday set up a dispute settlement panel to rule on a complaint regarding Hungary's agricultural subsidies. @
- A warning strike planned for today by workers at the power plant Matrai Eromu will not take place as the union has hammered out an agreement with the German owner.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Matra Defense of France has won the Defence Ministry's tender launched in 1996 to supply a short-range air defence missile system, announced Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will visit Washington on March 1-6. @

- US Ambassador in Budapest Donald Blinken told Reuters yesterday that in his opinion Hungary, along with Poland and the Czech Republic, is among the states that stand the greatest chance of being in the first wave of NATO expansion.
- After two weeks of plunging towards 21 percent, the annual average yield of one-month treasury bills edged up to 21.45 percent at yesterday's auction.
- Compensation coupons traded at record high prices at the stock exchange in the past two days, reaching a new high of HUF 840 yesterday. @
- After taking in HUF 25 billion in its giant issue of corporate bonds, the mobile phone company Pannon GSM has agreed to take up another $82 million in loans.
- The US aircraft manufacturer McDonnell-Douglas has opened an office in Budapest.
- KPMG Hungary will launch a new strategic consulting firm.
- An exhibition of Hungarian chemical companies will take place March 4-7 in Budapest. @

- Opera singer Karan Armstrong, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, Wiener Saengerknaben, and the Orchestra of Colours will be among the highlights at this year's Budapest Spring Festival beginning March 14.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- British Industry and Trade Minister Ian Lang will pay an official visit to Hungary on March 2-3.
- The gap between the purchasing power of Budapest and the country's other regions is widening, according to a study concluded by the Vienna-based consulting firm RegioPlan.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. may decide today to increase employees' salaries at companies it owns by 14-22 percent this year.
